Its exclusion (not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom, or for a role) does not apply: the words name the defined aggregate itself."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["dev.governs","dev.traffic_signal","dev.stop_sign","dev.yield_sign","dev.railway_signal_or_gate","dev.human_direction","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","rel.ahead_behind_in_lane","rel.surface_gap","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"],"derived":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'stopped or parked' is a vehicle brought to rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance' (a parked vehicle is at rest too, so the halt covers both words). The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'upon' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the whole way, as the atom does."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.lane","st.lane_marking","st.on_way","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"A highway 'where there are adjacent curbs' is one along which a curb runs: st.lane_marking gives 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}', so a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') with a side of type curb shows the curbs. st.road_edge is not used for presence: its contract is 'curb or edge of the roadway' and does not tell a curb from an uncurbed edge. st.lane is not a stand-in for a lateral position here: it is read only for its side marking."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["kin.heading","st.lane_direction","rel.occupies","st.travel_region","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"'parallel to ... the right-hand curb' with the right-hand wheels at it is a vehicle whose heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') lies along the designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of the travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), within a parallelism tolerance, pointed with that direction (the right-hand curb is the curb on the right of the direction of travel, so its right side faces it only when headed with it). 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side."},{"span":"s8","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","rel.occupies","st.one_way_roadway","kin.heading","st.lane_direction","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'adjacent' is read as alongside, parallel to the curb, the same position as subsection 1 states for the right."},{"span":"s9","atoms":["dev.regulatory_sign","dev.governs","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.parking_space","prim.conditions_hold","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"Angle parking permitted by the local authority shows on the road as an official traffic-control device: dev.regulatory_sign code 'angle_parking' governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), its 'structured conditions' holding (prim.conditions_hold), or a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's angle resolution. {"node_id":"NRS_484B_457_1","law_refs":["NRS-484B-457-1"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Except as otherwise provided in this section [(2) and (3) appended below],","role":"exception"},{"id":"s2","text":"every vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"stopped or parked","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s4","text":"upon a highway","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s5","text":"where there are adjacent curbs","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"must be stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s7","text":"Local authorities may by ordinance permit parking","role":"exception"},{"id":"s8","text":"of vehicles with the left-hand wheels adjacent to and within 18 inches of the left-hand curb of a one-way highway.","role":"exception"},{"id":"s9","text":"Local authorities may by ordinance permit angle parking on any highway, except that angle parking must not be permitted on any highway constructed and maintained by the Department of Transportation under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS unless the Department has determined that the highway is of sufficient width to permit angle parking without interfering with the free movement of traffic.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion (not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom, or for a role) does not apply: the words name the defined aggregate itself."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["dev.governs","dev.traffic_signal","dev.stop_sign","dev.yield_sign","dev.railway_signal_or_gate","dev.human_direction","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","rel.ahead_behind_in_lane","rel.surface_gap","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"],"derived":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'stopped or parked' is a vehicle brought to rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance' (a parked vehicle is at rest too, so the halt covers both words). The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'upon' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the whole way, as the atom does."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.lane","st.lane_marking","st.on_way","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"A highway 'where there are adjacent curbs' is one along which a curb runs: st.lane_marking gives 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}', so a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') with a side of type curb shows the curbs. st.road_edge is not used for presence: its contract is 'curb or edge of the roadway' and does not tell a curb from an uncurbed edge. st.lane is not a stand-in for a lateral position here: it is read only for its side marking."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["kin.heading","st.lane_direction","rel.occupies","st.travel_region","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"'parallel to ... the right-hand curb' with the right-hand wheels at it is a vehicle whose heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') lies along the designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of the travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), within a parallelism tolerance, pointed with that direction (the right-hand curb is the curb on the right of the direction of travel, so its right side faces it only when headed with it). 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side."},{"span":"s8","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","rel.occupies","st.one_way_roadway","kin.heading","st.lane_direction","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'adjacent' is read as alongside, parallel to the curb, the same position as subsection 1 states for the right."},{"span":"s9","atoms":["dev.regulatory_sign","dev.governs","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.parking_space","prim.conditions_hold","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"Angle parking permitted by the local authority shows on the road as an official traffic-control device: dev.regulatory_sign code 'angle_parking' governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), its 'structured conditions' holding (prim.conditions_hold), or a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's angle resolution. The presence of the device is the evidence of the permission and of its lawfulness, including the Department's determination for a highway it maintains (status reading): the words that limit where the authority may permit angle parking bind the authority, not the road user. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the permission of the place."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s7","id":"asm.left_curb_parking_permitted","meaning":"the one-way way at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which the local authority having jurisdiction permits vehicles to park with their left-hand wheels at the left-hand curb, as the map's reading records"}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[{"span":"s1","why":"The provisions the words point to are subsections (2) and (3), which are segments s7-s9 of this same text and are carried there as the exceptions of this node; the words add nothing beyond them, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read.","scope":"none"}],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is at rest at the observation (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); it occupies (rel.occupies) a highway region h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) some lane (st.lane) has a side whose marking type is curb (st.lane_marking); and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap.","obligation":"At that observation, with h re-bound as in the applicability (a highway the subject occupies on which a lane has a curb-marked side), one of three holds; otherwise the duty is violated. (1) Right-hand curb: the subject occupies a travel region r lying on h whose designated direction d (st.lane_direction) has a dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge region e (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way) is on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset of e below zero) at a ground distance from its body (st.region_geometry) of at most 18 inches (literal). (2) Left-hand curb of a one-way highway, where asm.left_curb_parking_permitted holds: the subject occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on h with heading·d at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge e lying on h is on its left (offset above zero) within 18 inches of its body. (3) Angle parking permitted: the subject occupies a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or it occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.queue_halt_gap","p.parked_heading_cos","p.parking_space_angle_resolution"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s6","why":"The wheels are not observed: the body outline stands for them. The wheels lie inside the footprint, so the body-to-curb distance is at most the wheel-to-curb distance and the reading is lenient by the wheels' inset (a few centimetres). 'parallel' is read within the tolerance p.parked_heading_cos, headed with the designated direction, since the right-hand wheels face the right-hand curb only so.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s3","why":"A halt in the stream of traffic (at a device that governs the subject's region, or queued behind another road user within the queue spacing) is read as not the stop the section speaks of; a halt mid-way through a parking manoeuvre is judged like any other halt.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s9","why":"The permission given by ordinance, and its validity on a highway the Department maintains, is read from the posted angle-parking sign or the angled bay marking: the presence of the device presumes the status.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s2","why":"The duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A vehicle at rest (kin.speed 0) for 30 s in the curb lane of a two-way highway whose rightmost lane's right side is marked type curb; heading along the lane direction; the right road edge lies 1.2 m from its body; no device governs its lane, nobody is ahead of it, no angle sign or bay, no left-curb declaration."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same vehicle at rest with its heading along the lane direction and the right road edge 0.25 m from its body."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"The vehicle moves at 10 m/s along the curbed highway (kin.speed 10)."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"As in forbid, but the source declares region outlines absent, so the body-to-edge distance and the lateral offsets are unknown.","masked":["st.region_geometry"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"The vehicle is at rest 1.5 m from the right edge in a lane governed by a traffic signal showing circular_red: a halt in the stream of traffic."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"compliant","narrative":"On a one-way roadway with asm.left_curb_parking_permitted declared true, the vehicle is at rest heading along the roadway direction with the left road edge 0.3 m from its body and the right edge 6 m away."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The vehicle is at rest in a parking space whose angle is 60 deg, heading 60 deg off the lane direction, far from the right edge."},{"name":"branch_4","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"The vehicle is at rest 2 m behind another vehicle ahead of it in the same lane, 1.5 m from the right edge: a queue halt."}],"literals":[{"span":"s6","text":"18 inches","value":18,"unit":"in"},{"span":"s8","text":"18 inches","value":18,"unit":"in"}],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.halt_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution","source":"proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; reused unchanged"},{"name":"p.queue_halt_gap","unit":"m","value":5.0,"convention":"the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue","source":"proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_52_030_A; reused unchanged"},{"name":"p.parked_heading_cos","unit":"ratio","value":0.97,"convention":"cosine of the largest angle (about fourteen degrees) between a standing vehicle's heading and its carrier's designated direction at which it counts as parallel with the edge and headed with traffic","source":"proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_52_040_A; reused unchanged"},{"name":"p.parking_space_angle_resolution","unit":"deg","value":5.0,"convention":"the bay angle at or below which a mapped parking bay counts as parallel to the curb rather than angled: the source's angle resolution for mapped bays","source":"proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_52_070; reused unchanged"}],"gaps":[],"gap_resolutions":[]}

The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side."},{"span":"s8","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","rel.occupies","st.one_way_roadway","kin.heading","st.lane_direction","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_457_1","law_refs":["NRS-484B-457-1"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Except as otherwise provided in this section [(2) and (3) appended below],","role":"exception"},{"id":"s2","text":"every vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"stopped or parked","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s4","text":"upon a highway","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s5","text":"where there are adjacent curbs","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"must be stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s7","text":"Local authorities may by ordinance permit parking","role":"exception"},{"id":"s8","text":"of vehicles with the left-hand wheels adjacent to and within 18 inches of the left-hand curb of a one-way highway.","role":"exception"},{"id":"s9","text":"Local authorities may by ordinance permit angle parking on any highway, except that angle parking must not be permitted on any highway constructed and maintained by the Department of Transportation under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS unless the Department has determined that the highway is of sufficient width to permit angle parking without interfering with the free movement of traffic.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion (not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom, or for a role) does not apply: the words name the defined aggregate itself."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["dev.governs","dev.traffic_signal","dev.stop_sign","dev.yield_sign","dev.railway_signal_or_gate","dev.human_direction","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","rel.ahead_behind_in_lane","rel.surface_gap","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"],"derived":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'stopped or parked' is a vehicle brought to rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance' (a parked vehicle is at rest too, so the halt covers both words). The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'upon' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the whole way, as the atom does."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.lane","st.lane_marking","st.on_way","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"A highway 'where there are adjacent curbs' is one along which a curb runs: st.lane_marking gives 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}', so a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') with a side of type curb shows the curbs. st.road_edge is not used for presence: its contract is 'curb or edge of the roadway' and does not tell a curb from an uncurbed edge. st.lane is not a stand-in for a lateral position here: it is read only for its side marking."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["kin.heading","st.lane_direction","rel.occupies","st.travel_region","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"'parallel to ... the right-hand curb' with the right-hand wheels at it is a vehicle whose heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') lies along the designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of the travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), within a parallelism tolerance, pointed with that direction (the right-hand curb is the curb on the right of the direction of travel, so its right side faces it only when headed with it). 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side."},{"span":"s8","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","rel.occupies","st.one_way_roadway","kin.heading","st.lane_direction","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'adjacent' is read as alongside, parallel to the curb, the same position as subsection 1 states for the right."},{"span":"s9","atoms":["dev.regulatory_sign","dev.governs","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.parking_space","prim.conditions_hold","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"Angle parking permitted by the local authority shows on the road as an official traffic-control device: dev.regulatory_sign code 'angle_parking' governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), its 'structured conditions' holding (prim.conditions_hold), or a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's angle resolution. The presence of the device is the evidence of the permission and of its lawfulness, including the Department's determination for a highway it maintains (status reading): the words that limit where the authority may permit angle parking bind the authority, not the road user. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the permission of the place."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s7","id":"asm.left_curb_parking_permitted","meaning":"the one-way way at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which the local authority having jurisdiction permits vehicles to park with their left-hand wheels at the left-hand curb, as the map's reading records"}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[{"span":"s1","why":"The provisions the words point to are subsections (2) and (3), which are segments s7-s9 of this same text and are carried there as the exceptions of this node; the words add nothing beyond them, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read.","scope":"none"}],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is at rest at the observation (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); it occupies (rel.occupies) a highway region h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) some lane (st.lane) has a side whose marking type is curb (st.lane_marking); and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap.","obligation":"At that observation, with h re-bound as in the applicability (a highway the subject occupies on which a lane has a curb-marked side), one of three holds; otherwise the duty is violated. (3) Angle parking permitted: the subject occupies a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or it occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.queue_halt_gap","p.parked_heading_cos","p.parking_space_angle_resolution"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s6","why":"The wheels are not observed: the body outline stands for them. The wheels lie inside the footprint, so the body-to-curb distance is at most the wheel-to-curb distance and the reading is lenient by the wheels' inset (a few centimetres). 'parallel' is read within the tolerance p.parked_heading_cos, headed with the designated direction, since the right-hand wheels face the right-hand curb only so.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s3","why":"Why a vehicle is stopped is not observed. A halt mid-way through a parking manoeuvre is judged like any other halt.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"s9","why":"The permission given by ordinance, and its validity on a highway the Department maintains, is read from the posted angle-parking sign or the angled bay marking: the presence of the device presumes the status.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s2","why":"The duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A vehicle at rest (kin.speed 0) for 30 s in the curb lane of a two-way highway whose rightmost lane's right side is marked type curb; lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_457_1","law_refs":["NRS-484B-457-1"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Except as otherwise provided in this section [(2) and (3) appended below],","role":"exception"},{"id":"s2","text":"every vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"stopped or parked","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s4","text":"upon a highway","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s5","text":"where there are adjacent curbs","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"must be stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s7","text":"Local authorities may by ordinance permit parking","role":"exception"},{"id":"s8","text":"of vehicles with the left-hand wheels adjacent to and within 18 inches of the left-hand curb of a one-way highway.","role":"exception"},{"id":"s9","text":"Local authorities may by ordinance permit angle parking on any highway, except that angle parking must not be permitted on any highway constructed and maintained by the Department of Transportation under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS unless the Department has determined that the highway is of sufficient width to permit angle parking without interfering with the free movement of traffic.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway"],"derived":[],"justification":"'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side."},{"span":"s8","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","rel.occupies","st.one_way_roadway","kin.heading","st.lane_direction","st.road_edge","st.on_way","st.region_geometry","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":[],"justification":"The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'those highways' (st.highway) is read as the part of the way the device governs or marks, where the angle it indicates is defined. Who controls the vehicle is read through its controlled motion."},{"span":"f3","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","dev.governs","dev.traffic_signal","dev.stop_sign","dev.yield_sign","dev.railway_signal_or_gate","dev.human_direction","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","rel.ahead_behind_in_lane","rel.surface_gap","kin.heading","st.lane_direction","st.parking_space","st.road_edge"],"derived":["drv.motion.complete_halt"],"justification":"'stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that. 'other than at the angle ... indicated by such devices' maps to its nearest atoms: kin.heading, st.lane_direction, st.parking_space, st.road_edge (see the gap). 'those highways' (st.highway) is read as the part of the way the device governs or marks, where the angle it indicates is defined. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that. 'other than at the angle ... indicated by such devices' maps to its nearest atoms: kin.heading, st.lane_direction, st.parking_space, st.road_edge (see the gap). The angle at which the vehicle meets the curb has as its cosine the dot product of its heading (kin.heading) with the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of the curb-side travel region; the angle the devices indicate is the bay's 'angle attribute' (st.parking_space), a number of degrees; the curb or edge is st.road_edge. The comparison of a cosine with θ needs the operator of the gap.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.queue_halt_gap","p.parking_space_angle_resolution","p.bay_angle_cos_tolerance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"f3","why":"The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception (traffic conflict, a device's or an officer's direction) read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing; reused unchanged"},{"name":"p.queue_halt_gap","unit":"m","value":5.0,"convention":"the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue","source":"proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_52_030_A; reused unchanged"},{"name":"p.parking_space_angle_resolution","unit":"deg","value":5.0,"convention":"the bay angle at or below which a mapped parking bay counts as parallel to the curb rather than angled: the source's angle resolution for mapped bays","source":"proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_52_070; reused unchanged"},{"name":"p.bay_angle_cos_tolerance","unit":"ratio","value":0.1,"convention":"the largest difference between the cosine of the angle at which a standing vehicle meets the curb and the cosine of the angle a marked bay indicates at which the vehicle counts as standing at the bay's angle: about six degrees at a sixty-degree bay, the placement variability of a vehicle within a marked angle bay","source":"angle-parking stall layout practice (stall angles of 30 to 90 degrees, with a few degrees of placement variability)"}],"gaps":[{"span":"f3","kind":"operator","proposal":"Term.cosDeg (a : Term) : the cosine of an angle a given in degrees, a ratio; unknown where a is unknown. It decides where the act is required: whether a vehicle stands at the angle the devices indicate, by comparing the cosine of its angle to the curb (the dot product of kin.heading with the curb-side carrier's st.lane_direction) with the cosine of the bay's angle (st.parking_space angle, deg).","nearest":"kin.heading and st.lane_direction give the cosine of the vehicle's angle to the curb; st.parking_space gives the indicated angle in degrees; no Term relates the two (no trigonometric operator), and an approximation by a table of literal angles would be a model the words do not state."}],"gap_resolutions":[]}

# Plan — batch 23 (NRS 484B parking: curb position, angle, night lamps, alleys, narrow and one-way highways)

No new concepts: every node reuses `drv.motion.complete_halt` or `drv.motion.parked` from this iteration. No law-local aggregates (`aggregates.jsonl` is empty). No composition: the library has no composable node, and no span of these laws names another rule. Every parameter is one an earlier batch proposed, reused with its value and convention unchanged, except `p.bay_angle_cos_tolerance` and `p.entrance_block_gap`, both of which are new and belong to gapped nodes.

**How "stop, stand or park" is read where it is prohibited (NRS_484B_460, NRS_484B_477_1a, NRS_484B_477_1b, NRS_484B_477_2).** The table resolves "stop" to two definitions, each with its own scope. Where stopping is prohibited, DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies: "any halting, even momentarily … except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device". Standing and parking are halts too, so the three verbs together are read as the halting they all are (`drv.motion.complete_halt`), with the stopping definition's exception carried by observable conduct:
- a halt in a travel region governed by a signal, a stop sign, a yield sign, a railway device or a person directing traffic; or
- a halt queued behind a road user ahead in the lane within `p.queue_halt_gap`.

This follows the index mapping of "shall not stop" (NRS_484B_413_3). The words "No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle" are mapped in the index to the halt alone (LVMC_11_52_130_A11). That node carries the exception on other spans of its own, which is why the device and queue atoms here sit on the obligation span. Each node discloses this as a narrowing. The signal that would reverse it: a labelled recording in which a vehicle queued or halted at a signal inside the regulated place is labelled violated.

**NRS_484B_457_1** — one obligation: the right-hand wheels parallel to the right-hand curb and within 18 inches of it. Subsections (2) and (3), which the text appends, are exceptions of this node.
- **Trigger.** "stopped or parked" is a halt (`complete_halt`). A halt made for traffic (at a device governing the subject's region, or queued) is read as not the stop the section speaks of. This is disclosed as an `observable_reading` of category `purpose`, since why a vehicle is stopped is not observed; DEF-NRS-484A-260 supports it. The validator refused a plain narrowing on the trigger.
  - Reversal: a label that treats a vehicle halted at a red light away from the curb as violating 457(1).
  - The words "stopped or parked" are mapped differently from the index (450_1l maps them to the halt alone): there they describe another vehicle; here they decide when the subject's duty arises.
- **Curbs.** "Adjacent curbs" is read from `st.lane_marking` type `curb`, because `st.road_edge` ("curb or edge") cannot tell a curbed edge from a plain one. The distance to the curb is measured to a road edge on the same way, on the subject's right.
- **Wheels and parallel.** The body outline stands for the wheels, which is lenient by the wheels' inset (a narrowing). "Parallel" means within `p.parked_heading_cos` of the carrier direction, headed with it.
- **Left-curb exception (2).** Permission by ordinance shows on no road feature, so it is the assumption `asm.left_curb_parking_permitted`, a legal designation of the way.
- **Angle-parking exception (3).** Read from the posted `angle_parking` sign or an angled bay (status). The words binding the Department and local authorities, on where angle parking may be permitted, are part of the device's presumed lawful status: they are carried inside that exception span, not as a road-user condition.
- **The opening words.** "Except as otherwise provided in this section" only points at (2) and (3), so it is a residue of scope `none`.

**NRS_484B_460** — planned but not codable: an `operator` gap.
- The vehicle's angle to the curb has a cosine (its heading dotted with the carrier direction), while the angle the device indicates is the bay's `angle` attribute in degrees. Term has no trigonometric operator, so the two cannot be compared. The gap proposes `Term.cosDeg`.
- The obligation words are one span (the validator requires one obligation span), carried by the halt plus the nearest atoms of the angle.
- "Those highways which have" devices is read as the region the angle sign governs, or an angled bay the subject occupies, where an indicated angle exists.
- Reversal: an operator able to compare the two, or an ontology row giving a bay's orientation as a direction.

**NRS_484B_473_2** — planned but not codable: an `operator` gap on "lawfully".
- "Lawfully parked" turns on the verdict of every parking rule the vehicle engages, and the words name none. `Formula.rule` composes one named rule. No published parking rule exists to compose either.
- The gap repeats the need of carried-over gap smoke31-1111-0039:G22 ("in compliance with law").
- The rest is planned:
  - parked: `drv.motion.parked`;
  - nighttime: `env.darkness`;
  - on a highway: `st.highway`;
  - lights displayed: headlamp or position lamp;
  - "cowl or parking lamps not used": the headlamps are lit. `sig.position_lamp` also lights with the headlamps, so it cannot tell parking lamps used in their place.
  - The duty is that the headlamp is not `high_beam`.
- Reversal: the operator retires G22 or decides this gap.

**NRS_484B_477_1a**
- "Unless otherwise provided by ordinance" is the assumption `asm.local_alley_ordinance`: an administrative designation of the alley, with no road feature.
- "In a business district" reuses `asm.business_district`.
- The standard "expeditious loading or unloading of goods" is operationalized by `drv.motion.parked` with `p.parking_min_duration`. The unobserved purpose is read through the halt's brevity: a halt beyond the temporary-halt bound is not excepted. This is disclosed on the standard span.
- Reversal: a labelled short halt without loading judged violated, which would call for door-open evidence (`sig.door_open`) instead of duration.

**NRS_484B_477_1b**
- "In any other" refers to paragraph (a)'s "alley in a business district". It is carried as `asm.business_district` not holding, so the alleys of (a) are left out with their qualification intact.
- The words "in such a manner, or under such conditions as to leave available less than 10 feet …" are a condition on the prohibited halt (the validator requires one obligation span).
- The free width is measured on each side of the body:
  - to the nearest road edge (ground distance, side from the lateral offset);
  - or to an obstruction or a halted member of traffic alongside on that side;
  - a side is free when everything on it is at least 10 feet away.
- "Vehicular traffic" claims the traffic and vehicle aggregates: members of traffic halted alongside narrow the width, and the width serves vehicles whether or not one is present.
- The obligation is the halt's prohibition, with the stopping definition's exception.

**NRS_484B_477_2** — planned but not codable: an `atom` gap.
- `st.driveway_or_alley_entrance` "does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's". Inside an alley it would mark the alley's own mouth onto the street, which is no "entrance to any abutting property".
- The gap proposes `st.property_entrance`.
- "Block" is read as overlapping the entrance's mouth, or standing within `p.entrance_block_gap` of it (newly proposed).
- Reversal: an attribute or atom telling property entrances apart.

**NRS_484B_490**
- "Devices … prohibiting parking upon a narrow highway" is the `dev.zone_sign` kind `narrow_highway` governing the subject's travel region, with its conditions holding. The highway's narrowness is the posting's designation, read from the sign (status).
- "Upon any such highway" is the same governed region.
- "Park" is `drv.motion.parked` with `p.parking_min_duration`.
- Reversal: if the narrow_highway zone sign proves to be a warning only, the trigger needs a no_parking regulatory sign inside such a zone.

**NRS_484B_493**
- Notice is read from:
  - a `no_standing` or `no_parking` regulatory sign whose conditions hold, governing the subject's region; or
  - a `no_parking` / `no_stopping` curb zone the subject occupies.
- "Street" is a highway inside a city (DEF-NRS-484A-265), carried by `asm.within_incorporated_city` on its own span. The way itself is carried by the one-way roadway it lies on.
- The left-hand side is relative to the roadway's designated direction: the subject is nearer a road edge on the left of that direction than every edge on its right. The side is taken from the lateral offset, signed by heading·direction.
- "Stand or park" is `drv.motion.parked` with `p.standing_min_duration`, following the index mapping of "No person shall stand or park a vehicle".

## For the operator

- Three nodes carry gaps and will not be coded until they are decided:
  - `Term.cosDeg` (NRS_484B_460);
  - a compliance-with-all-engaged-rules operator for "lawfully" (NRS_484B_473_2, the same need as G22);
  - `st.property_entrance` (NRS_484B_477_2).
- `asm.local_alley_ordinance` (new) and `asm.business_district` must be declared per map for the alley nodes. An undeclared assumption leaves their verdicts unknown.
- `p.parking_min_duration` (180 s) and `p.standing_min_duration` (60 s) are windows behind the observation. On recordings shorter than these windows, every long halt reads unknown, not violated.
- `st.lane_marking` type `curb` is the only atom that shows the presence of curbs in NRS_484B_457_1. A source that does not label curb-type lane sides leaves that law unknown.
